title: Etale comparison for dense extensions of henselian valued fields
statement:
Let $K\hookrightarrow K'$ be an inclusion of fields with nontrivial valuations, for which both valuation rings are henselian [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Suppose the valuation topology of $K$ is induced from that of $K'$ and $K$ is dense in $K'$: every nonempty ball $\{x:v(x-a)>\gamma\}$ meets $K$. Choose compatible separable closures $K^{\mathrm{sep}}\hookrightarrow (K')^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. The restriction homomorphism of absolute Galois groups with their Krull topologies is an isomorphism of topological groups:
$$\operatorname{Gal}((K')^{\mathrm{sep}}/K')\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K).$$
Consequently, for every torsion abelian sheaf $G$ on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and every $q\geq0$, the canonical pullback is an isomorphism
$$H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}},G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K')_{\mathrm{et}},G|_{K'}).$$
The maps are natural in $G$, with inverse image and cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No completeness, discreteness of valuation, or restriction on residue characteristic is assumed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: First prove that every element $a\in K^{\prime}$ separable algebraic over $K$ lies in $K$. Put $E=K(a)$. By [lem-per-henselian-finite-extension-topology], the topology on $E$ inherited from $K^{\prime}$ is the topology of the unique prolonged henselian valuation of $K$: the extension is finite separable, and its subspace topology induces exactly the given topology of $K$. Embed $E$ in a finite Galois $N/K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions], and prolong the valuation by [lem-per-henselian-finite-extension-topology]. By [lem-per-henselian-krasner-neighbourhood], a sufficiently small open neighbourhood of $a$ in $N$ consists of $b$ with $a\in K(b)$. Its intersection with $E$ is open. Since $K$ is dense in $K^{\prime}$ and $K\subseteq E\subseteq K^{\prime}$, $K$ is dense in $E$: an open subset of $E$ is its intersection with an open subset of $K^{\prime}$, and density gives a point of $K$ in that intersection. Choose such a $b\in K$. Then $K(b)=K$, so $a\in K$. This uses equality of valuation topologies, without silently identifying the two valuations on $K$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: Every monic separable irreducible $h\in K[T]$ remains irreducible over $K^{\prime}$. Indeed [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization] splits $h$ into distinct linear factors in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] says that this closure is separable algebraic and normal over $K$. If a proper monic factor of $h$ existed in $K^{\prime}[T]$, its coefficients, being elementary symmetric functions of a subset of the roots of $h$, would also lie in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Each coefficient is therefore separable algebraic over $K$ and lies in $K^{\prime}$, hence lies in $K$ by Step 1. This contradicts irreducibility over $K$. The same reasoning applies to the complementary factor. In particular, for a finite separable $L/K$, choose $L=K(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-primitive-element]; then $K^{\prime}\otimes_K L=K^{\prime}[T]/(\min_t)$ is a field, and its map into the compositum $K^{\prime}L$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: Fix $\theta\in(K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and put $L=K^{\prime}(\theta)$. If $\theta\in K^{\prime}$, it already lies in $K^{\prime}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$; otherwise its monic minimal polynomial $f\in K^{\prime}[T]$ has degree $n>1$ and $f^{\prime}(\theta)\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] take a finite Galois extension $N/K^{\prime}$ containing $L$. By [lem-per-henselian-finite-extension-topology] extend the valuation to $N$; its restriction makes $L$ henselian and induces the given topology on $K^{\prime}$. Choose the open Krasner neighbourhood $U$ of $\theta$ in $N$ supplied by [lem-per-henselian-krasner-neighbourhood]. Apply [lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability] over the henselian field $L$, to $f$, its simple root $\theta$, and $U\cap L$. This gives an open neighbourhood $V$ of the coefficient tuple of $f$ in $L^n$. Its inverse image in $(K^{\prime})^n$ is open and contains that tuple. A product of $n$ open neighbourhoods is contained in this inverse image; choose each coordinate in $K$ using density. We obtain a monic $g\in K[T]$ of degree $n$ with a simple root $\beta\in U\cap L$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: By the defining property of $U$ in [lem-per-henselian-krasner-neighbourhood], $\theta\in K^{\prime}(\beta)$. Since $\beta\in L=K^{\prime}(\theta)$, these two fields are equal. Thus the minimal polynomial of $\beta$ over $K^{\prime}$ has degree $n$, and divides the monic degree-$n$ polynomial $g$; hence it is $g$. Therefore $g$ is irreducible over $K^{\prime}$, and consequently over $K$. Since $g^{\prime}(\beta)\ne0$, irreducibility makes $g$ separable: a nontrivial common divisor of $g$ and $g^{\prime}$ would have to be $g$, impossible as its derivative is nonzero of smaller degree. The splitting of separable polynomials in [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization] implies that this particular $\beta$, a root of $g$ in the fixed overfield, lies in the embedded $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Hence $\theta\in K^{\prime}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Since $\theta$ was arbitrary and the reverse inclusion is part of the chosen tower, we have $(K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}=K^{\prime}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: Now identify restriction algebraically. Every finite subset of $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ lies in a finite separable subextension, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-primitive-element] makes it simple. By Step 2 its scalar extension to $K^{\prime}$ is a field, identified with its compositum. Thus the map $K^{\prime}\otimes_K K^{\mathrm{sep}}\to K^{\prime}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is injective: a relation involves finitely many elements and is already tested in one such finite subextension. Its image is a field, being the directed union of these finite-stage field images, so the image is the whole compositum. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)$ the map $1\otimes\sigma$ therefore acts on the compositum, sending $\sum_i a_i b_i$ to $\sum_i a_i\sigma(b_i)$; it fixes $K^{\prime}$ and has inverse $1\otimes\sigma^{-1}$. Step 4 identifies this compositum with $(K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}$, so this constructs an extension of $\sigma$. Conversely an automorphism fixing both $K^{\prime}$ and $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ fixes their compositum pointwise. Restriction is consequently a bijective group homomorphism.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: This bijection and its inverse are continuous for the Krull topologies. The inverse image under restriction of the subgroup fixing a finite subset $S\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is precisely the subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}((K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}/K^{\prime})$ fixing the same $S$, which is open. Conversely, express a finite subset $T\subset(K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}=K^{\prime}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ using finitely many field operations and coefficients from $K^{\prime}$ and a finite subset $S\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The extension constructed in Step 5 of any automorphism fixing $S$ fixes every expression in $T$. Thus the inverse image of the stabilizer of $T$ contains the open stabilizer of $S$, and is an open subgroup. Stabilizers of finite subsets form the identity-neighbourhood basis of the Krull topology; translations give continuity everywhere. This proves the asserted topological-group isomorphism.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, expansion of the forms-of-Krasner argument.

proof.text: Let $u:\operatorname{Spec}K^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $B$ be base change on the small etale sites. For each etale $K$-scheme $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] writes $X$ as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $K$ (apply it to the only point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$). On each such summand, a $K$-embedding into $(K^{\prime})^{\mathrm{sep}}$ lands in the specified $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$: a separable minimal polynomial over $K$ splits there by [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization]. Thus restriction and extension of the point maps give a natural bijection from the geometric fibre of $B(X)$ to that of $X$. The actions agree through the restriction homomorphism, because both send an embedding $j$ to $\sigma\circ j$. By [lem-exc-etale-field-gsets], the fibre functors on both fields are equivalences and identify coverings with jointly surjective equivariant maps. Restriction of discrete actions along the topological-group isomorphism of Step 6 is an equivalence, with inverse restriction along its inverse; open stabilizers are preserved. It follows that $B$ is an equivalence of categories preserving and reflecting covering families.

source.place: Tag 03QT (theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point), with field-etale classification Tag 03QR and covering description Tag 03QS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites] to the site equivalence $B$ of Step 7. Precomposition along $B$ is an equivalence of abelian sheaf categories. It is exactly $u_*$, since [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $(u_*F)(X)=F(B(X))$. The left adjoint $u^{-1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is therefore its quasi-inverse: the quasi-inverse adjunction has bijective Hom maps, and uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with the specified adjunction. Hence its unit $\eta:1\to u_*u^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Evaluating at the final object gives an isomorphism $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,F)\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K^{\prime},u^{-1}F)$ for every abelian sheaf $F$; it is precisely the pullback of sections given by the adjunction unit, not an arbitrarily chosen invariant-group comparison.

source.place: Tag 03A0 (lemma-equivalence); direct and inverse images as recorded in the cited definition nodes.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $G\to I^{\bullet}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions], the additive equivalence $u^{-1}$ carries it to an injective resolution of $u^{-1}G$. In every degree, Step 8 identifies the map of sections induced by $\eta_{I^r}$ with an isomorphism. Naturality of $\eta$ makes these degreewise maps an isomorphism of complexes. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology gives the required isomorphism for every $q\geq0$. By [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], choose the second resolution to be $u^{-1}I^{\bullet}$ itself and its comparison map to be the identity; the resulting cohomology map is exactly the canonical pullback in the statement. The resolution convention in that definition includes bounded-below injective resolutions as K-injective ones. Naturality in $G$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. This proves the torsion assertion (the argument actually works for every abelian sheaf), with no condition on residue characteristic.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NQ-340a701c9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the mathematics in full. The item statement is identical to the Q27 snapshot that created it, with the same stmt_deps, so it is not weakened. It matches ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374 (PDF p.380): for a dense embedding of henselian valued fields, Gal(K'sep/K') ≅ Gal(Ksep/K) by forms of Krasner. All nine steps are correct. Step 1 gets relative separable closedness from the topology clause, the Krasner lemma and density; the topology of E from N equals the one from K' by uniqueness of prolongation. Step 2 shows irreducibility is kept over K' via the splitting leaf and Step 1. Steps 3–4 approximate the minimal polynomial over L by simple-root stability and density, and Krasner gives K'(β)=L. In Step 4, irreducible together with g'(β)≠0 gives separability, also in characteristic p, so (K')^sep = K'K^sep. Step 5 identifies the tensor product with the compositum, and Step 6 gives Krull continuity in both directions. Step 7 makes B an equivalence that preserves coverings, through G-sets. In Steps 8–9 u^{-1} is a quasi-inverse of u_*, so the unit is an iso, and the def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback convention J=u^{-1}I gives the canonical pullback. All three new nodes are true and generic, and none restates a clause of the item. The topology node holds because a valuation topology inducing the v-topology is dependent with the prolongation, by a shared henselian coarsening and uniqueness over it. The Krasner node is the standard henselian proof (w∘τ=w). Simple-root stability is Newton's lemma for henselian fields of arbitrary rank. I found no duplicates: I searched Krasner, prolongation, henselian valued fields and every valuation node, including lem-trf-valuation-separable-closure-extension, lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height and lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension. Batch-5: def-trf-valuation-ring is the general definition from Stacks 00I9 and lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization is a generic IsSepClosed algebra leaf. Both are Mathlib leaves with only def stmt_deps, are outside the assumed trace-formula and Poincaré-duality statements and proofs, and are accepted. I accept the listed tool_uses. No SGA is cited. Advisory: the Krasner node leaves 'open in N' implicitly as the w-topology.
